Most homes along the Wasatch Front that still have their original windows are losing heat through them every winter and taking it on through the glass every summer. Replacement windows are the fix, and the difference shows up on the power bill. Every window is measured and ordered to the opening — there is no stock-size shortcut. Units come from Cascade Windows and Coeur d'Alene Window with Low-E coatings and argon gas between the panes, which is what actually cuts the heat transfer. You pick the vinyl color and grid style to match the house. Installation runs about 30 minutes to an hour per window, so most homes are finished in a day. We haul the old units out and clean up before we leave. A broken pane or a failed seal does not always mean you need a new window. If the frame is sound, the glass alone can usually be replaced — for a fraction of what a full replacement costs. Fogging between the panes is the most common call. That haze means the seal has failed and the insulating gas has escaped, so the window has stopped doing its job even though it still looks fine from across the room. Replacing the sealed unit restores it. We handle cracked and shattered panes, failed seals, and damaged sealant on both single- and double-pane windows. If the frame is too far gone to be worth repairing, we will tell you that instead of selling you a repair that will not hold.
